long_biography.plain_text:
Bernard Arnault trained as an engineer and rose through his family's construction company, redirecting it towards property development. After developing properties in the United States, he returned to France and acquired the bankrupt textiles group that owned Christian Dior. He retained the fashion house as the cornerstone of a luxury strategy. In 1989, he secured control of LVMH and built the group through acquisitions and patient development of individual houses.

Arnault has combined operational leadership with family control, remaining chairman and chief executive while preserving ownership through a family holding structure. His later cultural work took concrete form in the Fondation Louis Vuitton, a private art institution housed in Frank Gehry's glass-clad Paris building. Opened in 2014, it created a permanent setting for modern and contemporary art beyond the group's commercial houses.
